objective: Implement the FableCut-informed recommendations as a safe, client-neutral professional human-agent editing layer on Kacha's existing Timeline IR, and verify every locally solvable slice without weakening rendering, copyright, QC or human-review boundaries.
scopeIn: Workbench V2: direct manipulation, multi-select, snapping, trim, split, explicit EDL reorder, markers, work area, waveforms, keyframes, supported media replacement and delivery guides
typed operation commands compiled through the existing mutation and Command Journal path
revision-aware Studio editor events without a second state store
Project Bin backed by media index and corpus provenance
local technical rhythm analysis and rights-gated clean-room translation
client-neutral Kacha MCP stdio server with compact reads and typed operations
local MCP configuration metadata and deterministic first-run demo
focused, full, browser, protocol, security, documentation and installation verification
scopeOut: general-purpose NLE parity, whole-project JSON set or force overwrite
browser or WebGPU final rendering, cloud collaboration, accounts or remote asset storage
silent downloads, paid calls, external media upload or shot-for-shot reproduction
official MCP Registry publication, Git commit, push or GitHub release
creator-value claims without normal-speed human evidence
constraints: Timeline IR and 120000-tick Timebase V2 remain canonical.
Every edit requires base SHA, typed allowlist, atomic validation, journal evidence, undo/redo and required QC.
Workbench stays visibly approximate and cannot approve final render, QC or release.
Asset views disclose strong identity, provenance, license and semantic limitations.
Rhythm analysis is local technical evidence and cannot claim semantic understanding or creative authorization.
Public bundles exclude project/private assets and AppCreate evidence.
MCP filesystem access is restricted to an explicit configured project root and realpath containment checks.
assumptions: Supported media replacement preserves surrounding edits only for asset slots represented by current Timeline IR.
Waveform peaks can be generated locally with FFmpeg and cached by strong identity.
Protocol fixtures can prove current and legacy MCP compatibility without a runtime npm dependency.

architectureDecisions.decision: Add typed operation commands beside scalar changes, compiling both through one journaled mutation boundary; picture ordering uses an explicit reorder operation while timed tracks use bounded position changes; no UI-only edit state is persisted.

Represent markers, work area, keyframes and delivery frames as validated optional editor metadata inside Timeline IR 1.0; final rendering ignores metadata without execution semantics and parity tests prove metadata-only edits do not alter the Render Graph digest.

SSE carries only Timeline SHA and projection digest; browser access uses the unguessable active editor session handle because native EventSource cannot add the Studio header, while loopback Host/Origin checks and no-referrer policy remain mandatory.
Project Bin reads media-index/corpus contracts; insertion or replacement exists only for typed supported Timeline slots and must revalidate indexed SHA, provenance and license at mutation time.
Rhythm analysis emits cuts, onsets, BPM candidates, energy windows and drops; clean-room derivation remains rights-gated.
Use a dependency-free stdio MCP facade with deterministic tools/list, compact structuredContent, explicit project-root confinement, 2026-07-28 discovery and legacy initialize compatibility.
Distribution means bundle-contained metadata, configuration helpers and a local demo; external registry publication is an external condition.

rollback: Revert scoped source changes, restore prior Timeline/journal snapshots for experiments, remove only generated demo/temp/cache artifacts, and restore local skill targets from sync backups; never delete user media or silently rewrite client config.

findings.statement: Generic picture movement was incompatible with contiguous EDL semantics.
findings.remediation: Use explicit EDL reorder and reserve positional moves for timed tracks.

findings.statement: Editor metadata could accidentally be treated as rendered output.
findings.remediation: Validate it under an editor namespace and prove metadata-only changes preserve Render Graph digest.

findings.statement: Native EventSource cannot send the existing Studio read header.
findings.remediation: Use the active unguessable editor session handle with Host/Origin/no-referrer protections and negative tests.

findings.statement: Waveform work could block the server or consume unbounded resources.
findings.remediation: Require asynchronous FFmpeg extraction, capped bins, timeout, identity cache and bounded concurrency.

findings.statement: Arbitrary replacement paths would bypass asset provenance.
findings.remediation: Allow only current indexed assets and revalidate SHA, provenance, license and supported slot at mutation time.

findings.statement: A local MCP process without root confinement could expose unrelated files.
findings.remediation: Require an explicit project root and realpath containment for every file argument.

findings.statement: The phrase 90-second demo was ambiguous between media duration and activation time.
findings.remediation: Define it as a deterministic offline walkthrough completing under 90 seconds on the audited host.

adjustments: Replaced picture move with explicit EDL reorder.
Added render-digest parity for editor metadata.
Bounded waveform extraction and asset replacement.
